newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan Feb trade deficit falls to $207 mln. [CORRECTED 16:12 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Pakistan Feb trade deficit falls to $207 mln. [CORRECTED 16:12 GMT]

text.p: Pakistan's trade deficit fell to a provisional $207 million in February 1997 from $368 million in January 1997, compared to $264 million in February 1996, the Federal Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
Exports decreased 1.7 percent to a provisional $639 million in February from $650 million in January, and decreased 11.0 percent compared to $718 million in February 1996.
Imports decreased 16.9 percent to $846 million in February from $1,018 million in January 1997 and decreased 13.8 percent compared to $982 million in February 1997.

The trade gap fell (corrects from "increased") to a provisional $2.324 billion (corrects from $7.665 billion) in the first eight months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) from $2.361 billion (corrects from $7.418 billion) in the year-ago period.
Main exports were cotton yarn, fabrics, garments and rice. Main imports were machinery, chemicals and oil products. -- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
